MAE 2501 · Class B

Constant Force

Ions and Juggling Balls
Board — a = F/m
$\ddot{\underline{r}} = \underline{F} / m$
Integrate once: $\dot{\underline r}(t) = \dot{\underline r}_0 + (\underline{F}/m) t$
Integrate twice: $\underline{r}(t) = \underline{r}_0+\dot{\underline r}_0 t + ½(\underline{F}/m) t^2$
Practice 1

A ball is dropped from rest at height $h=2$ m. After how long does it land?

$$y = h - \tfrac12 g t^2 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; t_\text{land}=\sqrt{2h/g}$$

$h=2$ m $\Rightarrow$ $t=0.64$ s.

Practice 2

A ball is thrown straight upward from height $y_0=2$ m at speed $\dot y_0=5$ m/s. Find the airtime and apex height.

$$t_\text{air}=\frac{\dot y_0+\sqrt{\dot y_0^{2}+2gy_0}}{g},\qquad y_\text{apex}=y_0+\frac{\dot y_0^{2}}{2g}$$

$\dot y_0=5,\ y_0=2 \Rightarrow t_\text{air}=1.33$ s, $y_\text{apex} =3.28$ m.

Practice Problems

Practice Problem

A ball is launched upward at speed $\dot y_0$ from height $y_0$ in a constant gravity field $g$. Without solving for time, find its speed $\dot y$ as a function of height $y$.

$$\dot y\,d\dot y = \ddot y\,dy = -g\,dy \;\Rightarrow\; \dot y^2 = \dot y_0^2 - 2g(y-y_0)$$

$\dot y^2 = \dot y_0^2 - 2g(y-y_0)$ — speed falls with height, reaching zero at the apex $y=y_0+\dot y_0^2/2g$.

Practice Problem

The Moon has mass $M=7.3\times10^{22}$ kg and radius $R_\text{Moon}=1.74\times10^6$ m. What is $g$ at its surface? ($G=6.67\times10^{-11}$)

$$g=\frac{GM}{R_\text{Moon}^2}=\frac{(6.67\times10^{-11})(7.3\times10^{22})}{(1.74\times10^6)^2}$$

$g_\text{Moon}\approx 1.6$ m/s² — about one-sixth of Earth's.

Practice Problem

Two frames of that toss — the ball at its apex, and the same ball 0.25 s later. How big is the ball?

$$\Delta y=\tfrac12 g\,\Delta t^{2}=\tfrac12(9.81)(0.25)^{2}=0.31\ \text{m},\qquad d=\frac{\Delta y}{N_\text{diam}}$$

It drops about $3\tfrac14$ of its own diameters, so $d\approx0.31/3.25\approx9.5$ cm $\approx3.7$ in — a softball.
